battle.name: 征服
battle.brief: 前222年，秦王政於滅六國末段派軍平定江南：秦軍自關中南出，循漢水、淮水而東，以楚降卒充前鋒，攻破吳都姑蘇，吳王夫差自剄，越地會稽隨即入秦置郡。卡面的斯巴達長矛非本役制式裝備，是希臘方陣重裝步兵的兩米木槍；吳國自有的「攻敔王夫差矛」出土於江陵望山楚墓，可與本役長柄兵器互證。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 秦方是秦王政的中央軍國。滅韓、滅趙、滅魏、滅楚、滅燕的戰役都由關中涇渭一帶的郡縣徵發兵員，兵車、步卒、弩手合編，戰時歸大將節制，戰後歸郎中令、衛尉與各郡兵系統。滅吳越一役的主將一般記於王翦，參與者有王賁、蒙武、昌平君等；沿途所降楚卒被編入秦軍充當先鋒。秦廷的司空掌土木、舟車與轉輸，廷尉一系處理降附與詔令文書。吳方是吳王夫差的國家：都姑蘇（今江蘇蘇州），以重裝步兵、戈矛與強弓拒城，沿淮水至錢塘築有長城防線，水軍有大型樓船與鬥艦，舟師是吳國立國以來的老本行。越方是會稽一帶的越國，此時國力微弱，依附於吳，但仍保有自己的君長與部族武裝，吳亡後隨即被秦軍平定。同期地中海並非無事：羅馬正與迦太基打第二次布匿戰爭，希臘式重裝步兵方陣仍是那一帶的標準骨架，與秦軍的弩、戈與工程器材恰成兩種不同的步兵技術。
countriesEn: On the Qin side stood the centralised military state of King Zheng of Qin. The campaigns that destroyed Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu and Yan had all been fought with troops levied from the commanderies of the Guanzhong plain, the Jing and Wei valleys: chariot troops, infantry and crossbowmen were brigaded together, placed under a general's command for the duration of a campaign and handed back afterwards to the Court of the Langzhongling, the Weiwu and the provincial garrison system. The general credited with the conquest of Wu and Yue is usually Wang Jian, with Wang Ben, Meng Wu and the feudal lord Changping Jun taking part; Chu soldiers who had surrendered along the route were incorporated into the Qin army as spearhead troops. In the Qin administration the Sikong handled civil works, boats, carts and transport, while the Tingwei dealt with surrenders and the drafting of edicts. The opposing side was the state of Wu under King Fuchai: its capital was Gusu, in today's Suzhou in Jiangsu; it relied on heavy infantry, spears, halberds and powerful bows, and it manned a long defensive wall running from the Huai River to the Qiantang. Its navy included large tower ships and fighting galleys, and seamanship had been the old craft of Wu since the state was founded. The third party was the kingdom of Yue around Kuaiji, now greatly reduced in strength and dependent on Wu, yet still possessing its own ruler and tribal levies; it was subdued by the Qin army immediately after Wu fell. The Mediterranean was not idle either: Rome was fighting the Second Punic War against Carthage, and the Greek-style phalanx of heavy infantry was still the standard framework of armies in that region, exactly the opposite of the Qin combination of crossbows, halberds and engineering equipment.
people: 秦王政（嬴政）在位第二十五年下令平江南，此時他已滅韓、趙、魏、楚、燕，只餘齊國與江南未定。滅吳的主將一般記為王翦，一位六旬上下的老將，前224年破楚於淮水南岸的蘄地，傳說曾坑殺降卒數十萬，數字雖有爭議，他的戰績卻是秦廷倚重的招牌；其子王賁與蒙武等人負責追擊殘部及江南方向的水陸進軍，昌平君等封君亦與其事。吳王夫差是吳國主君，前495年即位，滅越後北上爭霸、前484年在黃池會盟諸侯，晚年卻要應付越人反攻。國破之時，據《史記》他「引刀自刺其頸」，歎曰「吾無面目以見子胥也」——伍子胥於他即位後第十一年被賜劍自盡，屍骨被盛入器皿示眾，吳人自此懼其鞭尸。吳國的實際防務由守城將領與長城線上的守軍分擔，舟師則由水軍官員統率。越國的君長在史冊中無名，只記其降於秦；秦軍所倚重的楚降卒姓名亦不傳，僅有「荊人降者」一類總稱。
peopleEn: King Zheng of Qin, personal name Ying Zheng, ordered the pacification of the south in the twenty-fifth year of his reign, by which time he had already destroyed Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu and Yan; only Qi and the lands south of the Yangtze remained. The general usually credited with the conquest of Wu is Wang Jian, a commander in his sixties who had broken Chu at Qi on the southern bank of the Huai in 224 BC; tradition says he buried tens of thousands of surrendered Chu soldiers, a figure that is much disputed, yet his record was the banner the Qin court relied on. His son Wang Ben, together with Meng Wu and others, pursued the remaining forces and led the waterborne and overland advance into the Jiangnan, and feudal lords such as Changping Jun took part as well. King Fuchai ruled Wu; he had taken the throne in 495 BC, destroyed Yue and then campaigned north to dispute hegemony, holding a council of the feudal lords at Huangchi in 484 BC, and in his last years had to face Yuean counter-attacks. According to the Shiji, when the city fell he drew his sword and cut his own throat, lamenting that he had no face to appear before Wu Zixu. Wu Zixu had been put to death eleven years after Fuchai's accession, and his bones were put in a vessel and displayed; the Wu people have dreaded the flogging of his corpse ever since. The actual defence of Wu was divided between the commanders holding individual cities and the garrisons posted along the long wall, while the fleets were led by naval officers. The ruler of Yue is nameless in the historical record, remembered only as one who submitted to Qin; the surrendered Chu soldiers whom the Qin army leaned on are likewise unnamed, appearing only in collective formulas such as the Chu people who had surrendered.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛是兩米上下的木槍，槍尾包銅箍套，是希臘重裝步兵方陣的標準長柄兵器，靠密集隊形與左翼扶盾互相保護發揮作用；它並不出現在前222年的華夏戰場上，本役可以對照的，是吳國自己的長柄兵器——「攻敔王夫差矛」，錯金鳥篆銘文，1982年出土於湖北江陵望山一號楚墓，今藏荊州博物館；同墓還出土越王勾踐劍，一支吳矛與一支越劍同埋楚地，正是吳越爭端留在考古層裡的痕跡。吳軍裝備以戈、矛、弓弩為主，戰士著皮甲、持大盾，長矛與戈併用是吳越兵器組合的特色；水軍有戈船、樓船、橋船之別，樓船高於望樓，弓弩手居高臨下射擊。秦軍這邊是弩機、鐵箭鏃、戈、矛、戟、盾與皮甲，秦始皇陵一號坑出土的干戈俑與弓弩手陶俑顯示其編制，兵車與載輜重的車牛同行，攻城則用雲梯、撞車與投石，都是前幾年攻楚時用過的裝備。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card, the Spartan dory, is a wooden spear about two metres long with a bronze socket at the butt; it was the standard pole arm of the Greek phalanx of heavy infantry, and it worked through dense formations in which the left-hand files shielded one another. It did not appear on any battlefield in China in 222 BC. The closest counterpart in this campaign is Wu's own pole arm, the spear of King Fuchai of Wu, whose gold-inlaid bird-script inscription reads that King Fuchai made this spear for his own use; it was unearthed in 1982 from the No. 1 Wangshan Chu tomb at Jiangling in Hubei and is now in the Jingzhou Museum. The tomb also yielded the sword of Goujian, king of Yue: a Wu spear and a Yue sword buried together in a Chu tomb are the very trace the rivalry of Wu and Yue left in the archaeological layers. Wu's troops were equipped with halberds, spears, bows and crossbows; the soldiers wore leather armour and carried large shields, and the combination of long spear and halberd is a hallmark of Wu-Yue arms. Its navy was divided into warships, tower ships and bridge ships, the tower ships rising above the fighting deck so that crossbowmen could shoot downward. The Qin army on the other side had crossbow locks, iron arrowheads, halberds, spears, tridents, shields and leather armour; the halberd-bearers and crossbowmen figurines from the first pit of the mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor show how it was organised. War chariots travelled with ox-drawn wagons carrying baggage, and for sieges the Qin used scaling ladders, battering rams and stone-throwers, all of them already used a few years earlier against Chu.
tactics: 秦軍的戰法是一條長距離的攻勢線：自關中取武關，順漢水、汝水向東，一路掃平楚地新附的城邑與殘軍，再折向淮水，渡江後沿太湖水網推進，攻取吳國設在長城線上的城邑，最後直抵姑蘇。糧道靠牛車轉輸，軍隊與輜重分隊而行，遇大澤就築橋、徵船；弩手在行軍縱隊中即以射擊掩護前進，遇城則集中弩陣壓制城頭，再以撞車與雲梯貼城。楚地降卒走在最前，他們熟悉江南水道與城防，可以引導攻城器械到位，這是秦軍第一次大規模以被征服者的兵作前鋒。吳軍以守城為主，沿長城節節抵抗，用弓矢居高臨下射擊秦軍先鋒，舟師則在太湖與江河中游弋，企圖切斷秦軍的糧道與渡口；秦軍的應對是分兵警戒水陸、以工兵保路，最後以圍城與夜襲破城。相較之下，卡面的斯巴達長矛代表的是另一種解法：方陣以盾牆在前、長矛越肩而出的密集隊形，強調正面撞擊與體力對耗，與秦吳之間「弩兵遠射、工兵破城、水陸分進」的攻城邏輯幾乎相反。
tacticsEn: The Qin method of war was a single long offensive line: out of Guanzhong by the Wuguan pass, downstream along the Han and Ru rivers, sweeping the newly seized towns of Chu and the last bands of Chu troops, then turning towards the Huai, fording the river and pushing through the water network of the Taihu lake, storming the towns that Wu held along its long wall, and finally driving straight at Gusu. Supply rode on ox-drawn carts; the fighting column and the baggage train marched separately, and wherever they met a marsh they built bridges and requisitioned boats. Crossbowmen already shot from the marching column to cover the advance; when a town came into view the crossbows were massed to pin the defenders on the walls while the rams and ladders were brought up to the gates. The surrendered Chu men marched at the head of the column: they knew the waterways of the south and the defences of its cities, and they could guide the siege engines into place. This was the first time the Qin army marched a whole conquest behind the soldiers of a conquered people. Wu fought mainly from its walls, resisting step by step along the long defensive line and shooting down from height at the Qin spearhead, while its fleets cruised the Taihu and the rivers seeking to cut the grain road and the ferry crossings. The Qin answer was to split the army to watch both land and water, to use engineers to keep the roads open, and finally to take the towns by blockade and by night assault. The Spartan dory on the card stands for a quite different solution: the phalanx massed behind a wall of shields with the spears levelled over the shoulder, a formation built for frontal collision and a trial of physical endurance, nearly the opposite of the Qin-Wu logic of long-range crossbow fire, engineer-driven siege and a combined push by land and water.
data: 時間：秦王政二十五年，即前222年，是滅六國戰役的倒數第二年；滅韓在前230年、滅趙在前228年、滅魏在前225年、滅楚在前224年、滅燕在前222年、滅齊在前221年。兵力：史書只說「二十萬」「五十萬」，前225年伐楚時王翦曾自請「非六十萬人不可」，數字多為誇大之辭，實數無從核對，但可見秦軍仍是關中一年能徵發數十萬人的兵制規模。路程：關中至姑蘇走漢水、汝水、淮水一路約一千五百至二千里，越秦嶺、漢水與江淮澤國。吳國疆域沿淮水至錢塘築有數百里長城防線，都城姑蘇在太湖東岸。人物年表：夫差前495年即位，前473年城破自刎，在位二十二年；伍子胥前484年被賜死。器物：望山一號楚墓出土吳王夫差矛一支、越王勾踐劍一支，皆為青銅錯金銘文器。月份：《史記·秦始皇本紀》對此役只記「二十五年」，不載月日，卡面所記月份為編排時的推定。
dataEn: Date: the twenty-fifth year of King Zheng of Qin, that is 222 BC, the penultimate year of the campaigns that destroyed the six states. Han fell in 230 BC, Zhao in 228, Wei in 225, Chu in 224, Yan in 222 and Qi in 221. Numbers of troops: the histories say only two hundred thousand or five hundred thousand; when he campaigned against Chu in 225 BC Wang Jian asked for no fewer than six hundred thousand men. Such figures are rhetorical and cannot be checked, but they do show that the Qin state could still levy tens of thousands of men from Guanzhong in a single year. Distance: the march from Guanzhong to Gusu by way of the Han, Ru and Huai rivers ran roughly one thousand five hundred to two thousand li, crossing the Qinling range, the Han valley and the marshy country between the two great rivers. Wu's territory carried a defensive wall of several hundred li running from the Huai to the Qiantang, and its capital Gusu stood on the eastern shore of the Taihu. Chronology of the men: Fuchai took the throne in 495 BC and died by his own hand when the city fell in 473 BC, a reign of twenty-two years; Wu Zixu was put to death in 484 BC. Objects: the No. 1 Wangshan Chu tomb yielded one spear of King Fuchai of Wu and one sword of Goujian of Yue, both bronze with gold-inlaid inscriptions. Month: the Shiji chronicle of the First Emperor records only the twenty-fifth year for this campaign and gives no month or day, so the month carried on the card is an editorial estimate.
cause: 秦滅吳越是統一大業的收尾，而不是一場偶發的入侵。前494年吳王夫差在夫椒大敗越國，把越王勾踐逼到會稽山中；此後二十多年吳國北上爭霸，前484年在黃池會盟諸侯，與晉國爭長。但吳國的強橫也替越人養出了死敵，勾踐臥薪嘗膽十年之後終於反攻，吳國的國力便耗在北方戰線與對越戰爭兩頭。楚亡之後秦的東進通道被打開，長江中下游的楚地剛被平定，人力物資尚未編制，正是最容易被吞併的時候；把楚地降卒拉去當前鋒，正是利用他們熟悉江南。吳國倚仗長城與水軍自守，不肯臣服，遂給了秦國一個「統一」的名分：秦王政要的不是吳國的土地本身，而是把齊、吳、越最後的抵抗一併清除，讓六國的舊疆變成秦的郡縣。
causeEn: The conquest of Wu and Yue was the closing movement of a unification already under way, not an opportunistic raid. In 494 BC King Fuchai of Wu crushed Yue at Fujiao and drove King Goujian back into the mountains of Kuaiji; for more than twenty years afterwards Wu campaigned north to dispute hegemony, meeting the feudal lords at Huangchi in 484 BC and contending with Jin. But Wu's arrogance also made a deadly enemy of the Yue people, and after a decade of hard training Goujian counter-attacked; Wu's strength was spent on two fronts at once, the northern commanderies and the war against Yue. With Chu destroyed, the road east lay open to Qin, and the Chu lands along the middle and lower Yangtze had only just been pacified, their men and goods not yet registered into the new order, which made them the easiest prey. Putting the surrendered Chu men in the van exploited precisely their knowledge of the south. Wu, relying on its wall and its fleet, would not submit, and that refusal handed Qin the name of unity: what King Zheng wanted was not Wu's territory for its own sake, but the removal of the last resistance of Qi, Wu and Yue so that the old lands of the six states might become commanderies of Qin.
impact: 此役之後，長江下游與太湖流域第一次被編入帝國的郡縣體系，秦置會稽郡，郡治在吳，後又置閩中郡，江南從此不再是化外之地，而是每年要繳糧、服役、徵兵的常態區域。吳越的青銅兵器傳統並未因此消失，吳越工匠的冶鑄技藝隨秦軍與移民南北轉移，漢代官營作坊與民間匠戶都承襲了南方鑄劍的風格。軍事上，秦軍摸索出一套可複製的帝國擴張模式：以被征服者的降卒充前鋒、以工兵保路修橋、以弩兵壓制城頭、再以郡縣接管城防；這套模式後來在北方、南方與西域反覆使用。戰略層面，吳越的舟師與長城防線第一次證明水網國家可以拖延正規陸軍，卻拖不過工程與後勤能力更強的一方。同期地中海的第二次布匿戰爭仍在進行，迦太基的象兵與羅馬的方陣相持不下，兩邊都在爭同一片海；前222年的華夏與地中海，都站在帝國化的門檻上。
impactEn: After this campaign the lower Yangtze and the Taihu basin were for the first time folded into the imperial system of commanderies and counties. Qin set up Kuaiji commandery with its seat at Wu and later a Minzhong commandery; the south ceased to be a country beyond the frontier and became a normal district that paid grain, owed service and furnished recruits every year. The bronze-working tradition of Wu and Yue did not vanish: the skills of the Wu and Yue smiths travelled north and south with the Qin army and with settlers, and both the official workshops of the Han and the village forges inherited the southern manner of casting swords. Militarily, the Qin army worked out a repeatable model of imperial expansion: the conquered men's surrenderers used as spearheads, engineers keeping roads and bridges open, crossbowmen pinning defenders on the walls, and then the commandery taking over the defences. That model was used again and again in the north, the south and the western regions. At the strategic level the fleets and the long wall of Wu and Yue demonstrated for the first time that a country of waterways could delay a regular land army, though not one with stronger engineering and logistics. At the same time the Second Punic War was still being fought in the Mediterranean, Carthage's war elephants and Rome's legions locked together over the same sea; in 222 BC both the Chinese world and the Mediterranean stood on the threshold of empire.
result: 前222年，吳國亡。姑蘇城破之後，吳王夫差自刎而死，吳國的政權連同其長城、舟師與城邑一起歸入秦國；秦軍繼續南掃，越國的君長歸降，會稽郡建立，郡治設於吳，秦的版圖第一次直抵錢塘江與會稽山。吳國的正式編制隨之解散：舊有將領多被分散編入秦軍各部，降卒與俘虜被分配到屯田與徭役隊伍中，吳越貴族有的被遷往關中。吳國的實際兵力與城防損失，史料沒有留下可核對的數目；《史記》對此只用「略定江南」四字。吳亡之後，秦只剩下齊國一個敵人，前221年王賁攻臨淄，齊王建出降，六國統一完成。次年秦始皇稱皇帝，郡縣制推向全國，而這場發生在江南水網深處的征服，正是統一的最後一塊拼圖。
resultEn: In 222 BC the state of Wu ceased to exist. After Gusu was taken, King Fuchai of Wu cut his own throat, and the polity of Wu passed with its wall, its fleets and its towns into Qin. The Qin army pressed south, the ruler of Yue submitted, and Kuaiji commandery was established with its seat at Wu, so that for the first time the Qin frontier reached the Qiantang River and the mountains of Kuaiji. Wu's formal military organisation dissolved with the state: its former officers were dispersed into the various Qin formations, surrendered men and prisoners were assigned to garrison and labour parties, and some of the Wu and Yue nobility were relocated to Guanzhong. No checkable figures survive for the actual strength of the Wu army or for its losses in the defences; the Shiji compresses the whole business into four characters, pacified the south. With Wu gone, Qin had a single enemy left, Qi, and in 221 BC Wang Ben attacked Linzi, the king of Qi surrendered, and the unification of the six states was complete. The following year the First Emperor assumed the title of Huangdi and carried the commandery-and-county system across the realm; the conquest deep in the water country of the south was the last piece of that puzzle.
